Hi team —

We started seeing a sustained jump in tail latency on your Hosted API for our production traffic since ~08:40 PST this morning. p95 has moved from ~120ms to ~850ms and p99s are now regularly > 2s; we also observed 502/504 spikes in our logs. This is impacting real-time flows (payment scoring) and causing retries.

I've attached a short trace and an example failed request (perf_trace_20270321.txt). Can someone please triage ASAP? We are prepared to accept a temporary routing to a lower-capacity endpoint or a short maintenance window if that helps.

Thanks,
Carlos

Thanks for flagging — I'm elevating to eng/SRE. Early notes:
- Symptoms smell like wake-path / pool-init lag: heatmap shows spikes aligned with autoscaler events for FinLogic's route.
- Priority: reduce customer-facing p95/p99 ASAP to avoid SLA credits.

Short-term mitigations to consider (need approvals):
1) Route 100% of FinLogic traffic to a warm, smaller-quantized model variant on already-active nodes (drop peak latency at cost of slightly lower throughput).
2) Temporarily increase pre-warm pool for FinLogic's region + enable active warmup probes (force model KV cache population at boot).
3) If above not feasible in <2h, apply rate-limited throttling with explicit customer notice to avoid cascading retries.

Attachments: runbook_wakepath_patch.md (small playbook, safe rollback steps).

Can @marissa and @grace confirm technical feasibility and estimated time-to-implement for (1) and (2)? If we need exec sign-off for cross-service routing changes I'll draft a short memo.

-Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:02:35 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Intermittent API timeouts + latency spike (FinLogic prod)

Quick scan of traces (attached) points to a wake-path stall where model warm-up is delayed by KV cache population + shard handshake times. Observed: node boot (t0) -> container ready (t0+6s) but model first-token latency not seen until t0+10-12s in many cases. This per-request late penalty multiplies at tail.

Immediate actions I can run now (10–15m):
- Flip FinLogic route to warm pool with preloaded quantized variant (redwood-alpine-8q). Will need a short routing change and traffic-test window of ~5m.
- Push a hotfix to autoscaler probes to force pre-warm cache fetch on instance start (non-disruptive, revertable).

If we do the route flip I recommend notifying FinLogic of planned 10m window and then observe p95/p99. If good, keep for 24–48h while we roll in probe changes.

Attachment: heap_snapshot_21mar.png; perf_trace_20270321.txt

-Marissa Cole
SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Exec summary: FinLogic production latency — request for temporary routing + credit approval

Team —

Summary: FinLogic (DL-8472) is experiencing p95/p99 regressions caused by wake-path initialization delays on our Hosted API autoscaling GPU pools. SRE identifies delayed model readiness (KV cache + shard handshake) as the primary contributor. Proposed immediate remediation: route FinLogic to a pre-warmed pool running the quantized fallback (expected p95 reduction from ~850ms -> ~140ms; p99 similarly improved). Rollbackable plan in runbook linked below.

Requests:
- Approve routing change to warm pool (estimated 15m ops work).
- Approve one-time customer credit for disruption (pro-rated daily usage) if FinLogic requests it post-mitigation.
- Exec visibility — FinLogic may request an SLA credit. We'll need to own comms.

If approved I'll instruct SRE to proceed and I'll coordinate customer updates.

Link to incident notes / runbook: https://drive.redwood/company/runbooks/wakepath-warmup

-Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability
